solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.meaning: to choose is to select one from several
the ... of the bunch is its finest member
a pointed tool for breaking ground or ice

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate definitions of one word: a verb meaning select, a noun for the finest of a group, and a digging implement.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word serves as a verb for selecting, a noun for the choicest item, and the name of a pointed digging implement.

clue.text: Stand in front of pavilion at Leeds ground

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here from pavilion
ground is the past tense of grind, so these letters are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A spectator stand in front of the cricket pavilion at Headingley in Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a cricket ground (Leeds has Headingley), but it is the anagram signal on AT LEEDS, giving EDESTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base or stand on which a statue or column rests.

clue.text: Film fan ordered nice high teas

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A movie buff asks for pleasant afternoon high teas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' only completes the surface phrase 'high teas'; the anagram uses just NICE and TEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is an enthusiast of cinema, a devotee of films.

parts.note: surpassing something is being above it
board is meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A dish that is better than ordinary fare and prepared to Jewish dietary law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kosher' looks like a food word joining the surface, but here it is the informal sense of legitimate or honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally kosher means genuine and legitimate, the same as an open, honest dealing.

clue.text: Fish in river swallowed by ray

indicators.note: being swallowed means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a ray of light is a beam

explanation.surface: A fish in a river is eaten by a ray, another fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like another fish beside the first, but here it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a freshwater fish of the carp family, also a name for some sea fish.

clue.text: Successes against Conservatives? Independent candidates initially restrained

indicators.note: restrained means held in, so the pieces sit inside the others

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party
I is the abbreviation for Independent, as on a ballot paper

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word candidates

explanation.surface: Election wins against the Tory party as independent candidates are held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Victories are wins or triumphs, a plain synonym for successes.

clue.text: Bribes help to bring in sponsors? Just the opposite

indicators.note: bringing in suggests one piece enclosing the other
this reverses the roles stated, so the sponsors take in the help rather than the other way round

parts.note: sponsors are financial backers
to give a hand is to help

explanation.surface: Bribes paid to attract sponsors, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the help would take in the sponsors; 'to bring in' plus 'Just the opposite' swaps which piece encloses which. Backhanders is British slang for bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is British slang for a bribe or illicit payment slipped to someone.

clue.text: In a jaunty manner, first-rate lines written about the Italian

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as the letters A and I

indicators.note: written about means set around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: RY, short for railway, stands for lines
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Breezily jotting down excellent verses about an Italian man.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, read as AI, is a crossword convention for first-rate; 'the Italian' is IL, Italian for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Airily means in a light, breezy, carefree way, matching a jaunty manner.

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or spread widely, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A dictator sent overseas on a posting.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, a synonym for tyrant.

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A talented daughter who has never married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accomplished' reads as skilled, describing the daughter, but it means completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accomplished has been finished, a past participle of the verb for completing.

clue.text: Block, centre reportedly for US government agency

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are spoken, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: a block is a piece, and a centre is a core

explanation.surface: A city block and its centre being the base of an American federal body.
explanation.definitionFit: The volunteer organisation founded under President Kennedy is an independent agency of the United States government.

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A crazy, peculiar character becomes a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the status of being a celebrated star, a close synonym for being famous.

clue.text: Challenges mother, unfortunately, over in African port

parts.note: to challenge someone is to dare them

indicators.note: over signals that the following pieces are turned round end to end

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Defying one's mother, sadly, in an East African harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the mother-and-sorrow pair round end to end to give SALAAM, an Arabic greeting. Dar es Salaam is Tanzania's main port.
explanation.definitionFit: Dar es Salaam is the largest city and main seaport of Tanzania on the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Old leader in tragedy greeting jealous husband

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from the word tragedy

parts.note: hello is a common greeting

explanation.surface: An ancient leading figure in a tragic play greets a husband consumed by jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice, who murders his wife Desdemona out of jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor kills his wife Desdemona in a jealous rage, making him literature's archetypal envious spouse.

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a change is an alteration
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A change in the use of clubs leads to a quarrel, perhaps at a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy dispute, a synonym for a heated argument.

parts.note: about means concerning or connected with
a revolution is a turn

explanation.surface: A parade-ground order linked to a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn is the drill order to face the opposite way.

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a referee judges a contest

explanation.surface: Indifferent to a cold-hearted judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central E of REFEREE, giving REFREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free from worry, so a carefree person is unconcerned.

clue.text: Person supporting that woman through a depression

indicators.note: being through something places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A woman who backs someone going through low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits, but is a hollow in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower who supports a cause, leader or party.

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trade union official gets the security word wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A SHOP STEWARD is the workers' elected trade-union representative in a factory or office.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop steward is the elected trade-union representative for workers at a workplace.

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashion models change their outfits only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means not often, an exact synonym for rarely.

definitions.meaning: to sieve or pass through a mesh

explanation.walkthrough: 'Air filter' reads as a car part; it is two separate definitions, a melody and to sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a passage of music, a melody, and to pass liquid through a sieve.

parts.note: auxiliary means additional or extra

explanation.surface: Taking a case away from a supplementary court.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to draw it out, so remove is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Severe, the south wind close to shore

parts.note: Auster is the Roman name for the south wind

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here from shore

explanation.surface: A harsh southerly wind blowing near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Auster was the Roman personification of the south wind; 'close to' can look like a link of nearness but takes the last letter of 'shore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern and plain, a direct synonym for severe in manner or style.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: an area is a field or department of activity
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Call any phone number in a department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is a circus or boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for contests, as a boxing or circus ring is.

clue.text: One who's often overly emotional in play group

parts.note: a play is a drama
Queen is the British rock group fronted by Freddie Mercury

explanation.surface: Someone in a theatre company given to tantrums.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama queen is an idiom for a person who habitually overreacts to small things with exaggerated emotion.

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is cut off the word

parts.note: to prime someone is to brief them in advance

explanation.surface: Plenty of the finest cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' reads as abundance, but it removes the last letter of BRIEF, the verb that 'prime' stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cow's milk cheese from the region of the same name.

parts.note: a statue is a kind of monument

explanation.surface: A huge sculpture standing beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Monumental means huge in scale, like a great memorial, hence massive.

definitions.meaning: a strip worn round the waist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a musical group with a hit record; the 's is just 'is' linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a strap round the waist and a slang verb for striking hard.
